source.title: Predicting Generalization in Deep Learning via Metric Learning - PGDL Shared task

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates combinations of model metrics as predictors of the training–validation generalization-gap ranking, using Kendall rank correlation. It does not test any version’s specific intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports the selected metric combination but gives no numerical correlation score. Individual metric inclusion settings are used to select the combination, so they are not separate result rows.
record.test_reason: The study predicts generalization-gap rankings using combined weight-change and learning-rate metrics. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or test any other claim version. References to original studies provide background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose automatic combination of simple metrics as a possible starting point for predicting generalization and observe that similar combinations usually score similarly. They also identify restrictions on metric scaling and increasing search cost as limitations. The abstract reports eighth place in the competition.
record.recipe_differences: A metric-learning competition submission combining model properties to predict generalization-gap rankings; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected combination includes Learning rate distance and Non-uniform weights and inverts Learning rate mean; the paper says similar combinations usually score similarly but gives no scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Automatic selection favored including Learning rate distance and Non-uniform weights, inverting Learning rate mean, and excluding the remaining metrics. No numerical correlation or individual-metric comparison is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A selected combination of training-dynamics and weight-change metrics can predict generalization-gap rankings on the competition dataset; its predictive strength remains unquantified in this report.

record.problems: The paper gives no numerical score for the selected combination, dataset details, or uncertainty estimates; the combination was selected by testing 2187 alternatives on the provided dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No other result rows extracted. The individual metric inclusion settings were used to select the best combination, rather than reported as separate outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.

Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking performance relative to norm and margin measures. Weight-change and learning-rate metrics do not measure this sharpness.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is warranted for V7 merely because the study shares its generalization-gap prediction objective or cites its original source. The paper provides neither a magnitude-aware sharpness measurement nor a comparison testing that version.

versions.untested_parts: Network width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and their held-out performance.
Large versus small batch sizes and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and its effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its comparison with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: the proposed metric combination
rows.stage_stated: trained models in the provided dataset; training details not stated
rows.operation_detail: Combined transformed metric scores to rank models by predicted generalization; selected the combination with the highest Kendall rank-correlation score.

conditions.value: provided competition dataset; details not stated
Learning rate distance and Non-uniform weights included; Learning rate mean inverted; other metrics excluded

rows.measure: Kendall rank correlation between predicted ranking and empirical generalization-gap ranking
rows.value: highest score among tested combinations; numerical score not stated
rows.note: One result for the selected combination; the paper does not give the score or separate results for individual metrics.
rows.check: This is selection of the study's own metric combination among 2,187 candidates, not a result testing a claim version, and should not be a claim-result row. The selected combination is reported correctly, but no correlation value is supplied; being the highest-scoring combination does not establish predictive accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
